message.content:
I don’t have a way to directly measure your connection from here, but you can quickly find out your current internet speed yourself. Here’s how:

### 1. Use an Online Speed Test
- **Speedtest by Ookla** – Visit [speedtest.net](https://www.speedtest.net/) and click “Go.”  
- **Fast.com** – Go to [fast.com](https://fast.com/); it automatically starts measuring your download speed.  
- **Google Speed Test** – Search “internet speed test” on Google; the built‑in test will appear at the top of the results.

These sites will give you:
- **Download speed** (how fast data comes to you)
- **Upload speed** (how fast data goes from you)
- **Ping/latency** (how quickly your device communicates with the server)

### 2. Command‑Line Tools (for tech‑savvy users)

#### Windows
```powershell
# Install PowerShell module
Install-Module -Name Posh-SSH -Force

# Run a simple speed test via PowerShell (requires internet access)
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://www.speedtest.net/api/api.php?format=json | ConvertFrom-Json
```

#### macOS / Linux
```bash
# Install speedtest-cli
sudo apt-get install speedtest-cli   # Debian/Ubuntu
brew install speedtest-cli           # macOS with Homebrew

# Run the test
speedtest
```

### 3. Check Your Router’s Admin Page
Most routers display current throughput statistics in their admin interface. Log into your router (usually `192.168.0.1` or `192.168.1.1`) and look for a “Status” or “Diagnostics” section.

---

**Tip:** If you’re consistently seeing speeds far below what your ISP promises, try:
- Rebooting your modem/router.
- Connecting via Ethernet instead of Wi‑Fi.
- Checking for firmware updates.
- Contacting your ISP for support.

Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the results or troubleshooting!
